speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To understand what is happening, let's start with your history: How long have these symptoms been present, and did anything specific trigger them, like a recent injury or new medication?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme disease (Borrelia burgdorferi) arthritis.

Based on your recent camping trip in Minnesota, the preceding self-resolving knee pain, and the new onset of wrist pain with fever, I suspect a tick-borne infection affecting your joints. Has the skin lesion appeared at the site of a bite on your body, and do you recall any ticks during your trip?
